text.p: The government posted a budget deficit of $40.26 billion in October, the Treasury Department said Friday, up from a deficit of $22.58 billion in October 1995.
October marked the first month of the government's 1997 fiscal year.
In September, the budget was in surplus by $35.43 billion. That figure was revised from a previously reported $35.37 billion.
White House officials are hoping to reach an accord early next year with the Republican-led Congress on a plan to eliminate the deficit by 2002.
The new Congress will convene in early January and President Clinton has expressed hope Republicans and Democrats can pick up where they left off earlier this year in budget talks.
The total deficit for the fiscal year ended September 30 1996 was revised to $107.26 billion, from a previously reported $107.33 billion. The fiscal 1995 deficit stood at $163.92 billion.
During October, total spending rose to $140.21 billion while income fell to $99.95 billion.

For all of fiscal year 1996, total government spending increased to $1.56 trillion from $1.52 trillion in fiscal 1995. Total receipts, largely from taxes, rose to $1.45 trillion from $1.35 trillion in fiscal 1995.
